findings.summary: A 45 rpm adapter is a small insert placed in the center spindle hole of a 45 rpm record, allowing it to be played on a turntable's standard spindle. Adapters vary from single-record solid inserts to larger multi-record spindles. Early versions were metal and difficult to remove; later plastic "spider" inserts became common. The SX2 adapter, designed by DJ Mark McLaughlan in the 1980s-90s, was created to facilitate handling 7-inch discs during mixing and is now a rare collector's item.

mechanisms.title: Spindle Fit Insertion
mechanisms.explanation: The adapter fits into the large spindle hole of a 45 rpm record, reducing its diameter to match the smaller spindle size of a standard turntable, thereby enabling playback.

mechanisms.title: Stack Play Adapter
mechanisms.explanation: Larger adapters fit over the entire spindle of a record changer, permitting a stack of 45 rpm records to be played sequentially.
